content.title: SIGNS YOU'RE ACTUALLY LOW ON {{IODINE}} (NOT JUST TIRED)
facts: **Neck swelling** – A subtle puffiness or tightness near your throat can signal your thyroid is straining without enough iodine to work with.
**Brain fog** – Feeling mentally slow or forgetful even after good sleep can point to low iodine, since your thyroid hormones help run your brain's energy use.
**Cold hands and feet** – Constantly feeling cold, even in a warm room, can mean your metabolism has slowed down from an underactive thyroid.
**Dry, flaky skin** – Skin that stays dry no matter how much lotion you use can be a quiet sign your thyroid hormone levels are off.
**Unexplained weight gain** – Slowly gaining weight without eating more can be your body's metabolism downshifting from an iodine shortfall.
**Hair thinning** – Hair that sheds more than usual, especially at the outer eyebrows, is a classic overlooked iodine-deficiency clue.
**Heavy, irregular periods** – Cycles that suddenly become heavier or unpredictable can be tied to thyroid hormone imbalance from low iodine.
**Fatigue that sleep doesn't fix** – Waking up tired even after 8 hours can mean your thyroid isn't getting what it needs to regulate your energy.

content.caption:
If you're constantly cold, foggy-headed, or your hair seems thinner lately, it might not be stress or aging — it could be your iodine levels. Iodine is the raw material your thyroid uses to make hormones that control your metabolism, so even a mild shortage can slow everything down, from your energy to your body temperature. The neck swelling some people notice is actually your thyroid physically enlarging (a goiter) as it tries to work harder with less iodine to use. And that stubborn dry skin? It happens because thyroid hormone helps regulate skin cell turnover, so when levels dip, your skin renews itself more slowly and holds onto moisture less. Everyone's body responds differently, so it's worth paying attention to your own patterns rather than comparing to others.

At @smarthealthfix, we break down nutrition, common symptoms, organ health, and small daily habits that actually make a difference. Our goal is to help you notice what your body is telling you before small issues become bigger ones.
